title: Extraction of Surface-Community DNA from Ulva sp.
author: Torsten Thomas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f3xbqpn
materials: Extraction of surface-community DNA from Ulva sp

Materials: - plastic bag/ container - washing bowl/ container - ice bucket sterile knife/ surgical blade sterile forceps 1 litre of autoclaved calcium- and magnesium-free sea water (CMFSW) recipe: 25 g NaCl 8 g KCl 1 g Na2SO4 04 g NaHCO3 distilled water to 1 litre live stain (1:500 diluted in CMFSW) tissue balance petri dish sterile 50mL Falcon tubes 3M Multi Enzyme Cleaner (sterile-filtered) large pipette tips (5ml) and pipettor sterile SS34 tube 95 % ethanol 70% ethanol 3M Sodium acetate (pH 5.2) TE-buffer Sterile water 2 ml microcentrifuge tubes

steps.title: Collect and prepare Ulva material
steps.instruction: Collect several Ulva sp. plants by hand from an intertidal pool, place them in a plastic bag or container with seawater from the same site, bring to the laboratory as soon as possible, transfer plants into a sterile washing bowl with a small amount of CMFSW, cut off the bottom 2–3 cm with a sterile knife and forceps, and chop the remaining thallus into pieces roughly 2–4 cm in length and width.

steps.title: Wash plant pieces
steps.instruction: Wash the plant pieces three times, each wash lasting 1–2 minutes with CMFSW, ensuring that smaller fragments and non‑plant material are removed.

steps.title: Microscopic surface assessment
steps.instruction: Take a couple of random pieces, place each on a glass slide, add approximately 10 µl of live stain, cover with a cover slip, blot excess liquid with tissue, observe under a fluorescent microscope, and record the surface coverage of cells.

steps.title: Weigh and incubate with enzyme cleaner
steps.instruction: Weigh 12 g of wet‑weight Ulva (drip‑dry) into a petri dish, transfer the 12 g into a sterile 50 ml Falcon tube containing 30 ml CMFSW and 300 µl of 3 M Multi‑Enzyme Cleaner, shake gently to cover the plant surface, incubate at room temperature, perform microscopy after 30 min; if few cells remain, proceed to the next step, otherwise continue incubation for a total of 1–2 hours until most surface cells are removed.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and filter
steps.instruction: Transfer the incubation liquid into one or two new 50 ml Falcon tubes (no more than 20 ml per tube), ensuring no plant material is carried over; optionally filter the liquid through a sterile 125 µm sieve or a 0.8 µm filter.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) to the supernatant, shake gently but thoroughly, centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 × g, and transfer the aqueous phase into an SS34 tube.

steps.title: First ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: To the aqueous phase add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate and 3 volumes of 95 % ethanol, shake gently (a white precipitate appears), incubate at –20 °C for at least 2 hours, centrifuge 30 min at 20 000 × g, discard supernatant, add 10 ml 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 5 min at 20 000 × g, discard supernatant, air‑dry the pellet, resuspend in 0.5 ml sterile water and transfer to a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Second ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate and 3 volumes of 95 % ethanol to the resuspended pellet, shake gently (white precipitate visible), incubate at –20 °C for at least 2 hours, centrifuge 30 min at 20 000 × g, discard supernatant, add 1 ml 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 5 min at 20 000 × g, discard supernatant, air‑dry the pellet, and finally resuspend in 50–100 µl TE‑buffer.

steps.title: Assess DNA on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load approximately 1 µl of the final DNA solution onto an agarose gel and run electrophoresis to evaluate DNA quality and quantity.
